newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks grip gains to close higher.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks grip gains to close higher.

text.p: The Australian share market kept a firm grip on its gains to close higher on Wednesday with options-related trade ahead of Thursday's January expiry and well-received inflation data underpinning the rise.
The All Ordinaries index added 10.0 points to 2,414.2.
While the fourth quarter inflation numbers were right on market expectations, brokers said the figures painted a picture of continuing low inflation, which heartened traders.
"It was basically on expectations," said dealer Nick Atkinson of Brisbane-based brokerage, Wilson HTM, adding that while the Dow was down, the market had largely ignored the negatives.
"Our market is looking for the positives," he said, pointing to a relatively strong gold sector which finished barely a whisker lower, despite a sharply weaker bullion price.
"You would have thought gold would have weighed on the market today but it has been a fantastic performance."
Resolute Samantha shares, up 2.3 percent to A$2.63 (US$2.02), and Eagle Mining scrip, up 1.5 percent to A$2.64, led the gold sector's resilient showing.

The big banks impressed before profit-taking set in. Westpac shares were the pick, up 2.3 percent to A$7.51, with several traders suggesting its strength came from options plays ahead of Thursday's January series options expiry.
Rises slightly shaded falls, while 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
